title: affinity-threshold-regressor-and-stochastic-cache-prioritizer
author: Evan Brooks
description:
Background and motivation:
We observed that tenant-level batch shaping and cache eviction heuristics tuned by static rules underperform on multi-tenant workloads with variable tail latency and heterogeneous prompt lengths. This PR introduces a compact threshold regressor to predict per-tenant batch/latency thresholds and a lightweight stochastic cache prioritizer that converts the regressor output into eviction weights and prefill priorities. The goal is automated defaults that reduce token-unit cost without violating latency SLOs, and to provide safe rollout controls for canarying and rollback.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Add threshold regressor training and inference code (small XGBoost-style gradient regressor implemented in Rust bindings + Python orchestrator) to predict an "affinity threshold" used by the batch shaper to decide microbatch grouping.
- Implement stochastic-cache-prioritizer: a probabilistic prioritizer for KV cache retention using an exponential weight derived from predicted affinity, recency, and unit-econ score. Allows soft fallbacks to LRU for tenants with insufficient telemetry.
- Introduce a cost-sim CLI (cost-whatif) to simulate per-tenant unit-econ impact of candidate thresholds/TTL profiles across a sampled replay window. Useful for ops and SRE reviews and for generating presets.
- Add runtime flags and a feature-flag gating flow: canary percentage, tenant-whitelist, and safe-fallback to current rule-based behavior.
- Integrate telemetry: new metrics (cost_unit_delta, affinity_confidence, stochastic_eviction_rate) and dashboards. Add tracing spans around regressor inference and cache decisions.
- Tests and perf checks: unit tests for regressor serialization, simulation dry-run mode, and a canary e2e that runs on the perf-lab harness with synthetic load.

Checklist:
- [x] Training pipeline + model artifacts export
- [x] Inference path integrated into batch shaper
- [x] Probabilistic cache prioritizer with LRU fallback
- [x] CLI simulate and export presets
- [x] Metrics, traces, and dashboards updated
- [x] Canary rollout plan documented in PR + runbook link
- [x] Unit + integration tests added

Commit summary (high-level):
- feat(cost): add affinity threshold regressor training pipeline and model format
- feat(runtime): wire regressor inference into batch shaper decision path
- feat(cache): implement stochastic-cache-prioritizer with LRU fallback and TTL blending
- feat(cli): add cost-whatif simulation CLI and export-presets subcommand
- perf(tests): add perf-lab canary harness scenarios and synthetic replay traces
- docs: add runbook and runbook examples for safe rollback and canary metrics

Files changed (high-level):
- services/cost-optimizer/regressor/train.py - training orchestration and feature extraction
- services/cost-optimizer/regressor/format.rs - compact model serialization + rust inference shim
- runtime/serving/batcher/affinity_shaper.rs - integrate regressor inference and threshold application
- runtime/cache/stochastic_prioritizer.rs - core prioritizer + LRU fallback code
- tools/cost-whatif/cli.py - simulate and export presets
- telemetry/metrics/cost_metrics.yaml - new metric defs and dashboard fragments
- docs/runbooks/cost_automations_canary.md - canary plan and rollback steps
- tests/unit/test_regressor_serialization.py, tests/e2e/perf/canary_affinity_scenarios.yaml

Small illustrative snippet (core scoring function in pseudocode):
- weight = exp(beta * predicted_affinity) * (1 - recency_factor) * unit_econ_scale
- eviction_prob = normalize(weight over candidate keys)
(implemented in stochastic_prioritizer.rs as 28-line function; fallback to LRU when confidence < 0.2)

Rollout plan and risk controls:
- Feature flag gated behind ff/cost/affinity-regressor; default off.
- Canary: start at 5% tenant traffic (tenant whitelist) -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 24hr observation windows.
- Auto-fallback: if cost_unit_delta > 10% increase or p95_latency regresses by > 5% during canary window, flag auto-rollback to LRU path and alert SRE.
- Presets export: ops can run cost-whatif on historical traces to generate tenant-specific safe thresholds.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Added Grafana panels for cost_unit_delta (by tenant), affinity_confidence distribution, stochastic_eviction_rate, and canary cohort comparisons.
- Added tracing spans: regressor.infer, shaper.evaluate, prioritizer.select_key.

Testing notes and CI:
- Local unit test coverage: regressor serialization, scoring monotonicity, CLI dry-run outputs.
- Perf-lab e2e: synthetic replay for heavy and mixed prompt-length tenants; compares baseline LRU + static thresholds vs new regressor flow.
- CI: lint -> unit tests -> integration on emulator -> perf-lab smoketest. All checks passed on the final push.

Why this is different from previous work:
Previous PRs focused on static presets, batch templates, or greedy cache heuristics. This change adds a compact learned regressor (small-footprint) and couples it to a probabilistic prioritizer; it emphasizes safe canarying and a what-if simulator so ops can observe unit-econ tradeoffs before enabling at scale. The regressor is deliberately small to make inference cheap and predictable, preventing regressor compute from offsetting token savings.

Known limitations and follow-ups:
- Current regressor uses light-weight tree ensembles; plan to evaluate a distilled neural model if accuracy/benefit justify cost.
- Need more tenant-segmentation features in feature extraction for nuanced enterprise traffic patterns.
- CLI currently works on exported traces; integrating a stream-mode replay is planned (ENG-4688).

- ENG-4688: integrate streaming-sim with cost-whatif
- SUP-789: customer feedback about unexpected cache churn on high-variance tenants
